title: AI Instagram Ads for Reels, Stories and Feed | AIVideosUGC
description: Make AI Instagram ads from a single product photo: 9:16 clips for Reels and Stories plus square visuals for the feed. Check the cost first, then create yours.
h1: AI Instagram Ads From the Product Photos You Already Have
lead: Turn one photo into a vertical clip for Reels and Stories or a square post for the feed, then add your caption and offer in Instagram or Ads Manager.
card: Vertical clips for Reels and Stories, square posts for the feed.
intro: Instagram ads show up in three main spots: Reels, Stories and the feed. Reels and Stories fill the whole phone screen, while the feed sits between posts from friends and creators, so an ad has to look at home in each. AIVideosUGC makes 9:16 videos for Reels and Stories and 1:1 videos for the feed, each running 6, 10 or 15 seconds. You can also create square product images for feed posts and carousels.

Upload your product shot along with a line about the setting: a serum bottle on a marble sink, sunglasses on a beach towel, a candle beside an open book. The result comes back to your account, private to you. Download it, write your caption, and add any text or stickers in Instagram, Canva or Ads Manager.
tips: In Stories and Reels, leave breathing room at the top and bottom, because the profile name, reply bar and caption cover those areas.
Center the product so it still reads clearly when Instagram crops the preview on your profile grid or in Explore.
Match the light and colors of your regular posts so the ad feels like part of your account rather than an interruption.

ideas.d: A vertical clip that starts on the closed box and ends on the product, made for a tap-through Story ad.
Create a few square images one by one, such as a front view, the item in hand and the item on a shelf, and post them together as a carousel.
Show sneakers on a city sidewalk or a tote bag on a cafe chair so the product feels like part of someone's day.

faq.q: How can I check an Instagram ad before publishing?
faq.a: Preview the asset in its intended placement and check that captions, reply areas, and profile controls do not cover key product details.

faq.q: Can I use one video for both Stories and Reels?
faq.a: Yes, both use the full vertical screen. Keep the product near the middle, because each placement covers the edges in slightly different ways.

faq.q: Can AIVideosUGC add my logo or a discount code?
faq.a: Add them yourself after download in Canva, CapCut or Ads Manager. Lettering drawn by AI can come out misspelled, so placing it yourself is safer.

faq.q: Will my product photos appear on Instagram or anywhere public?
faq.a: No. Everything you upload or create is kept private in your account. Nothing goes on Instagram unless you post it.

overview.h2: Make a set that belongs together
overview.d: A consistent background and color palette can make a set of Instagram posts look like one campaign. Start with the product photo that best shows its shape, then describe one setting for a square feed image and another for a 9:16 Reel or Story. Keep the color and surface related across the set so the still post and the moving clip look like the same campaign, even when each is generated separately.

overview.h2: Design for Reels, Stories, and the feed separately
overview.d: Meta's Reels guidance recommends 9:16 and keeping important content inside the safe area. Preview each downloaded file in its intended placement before adding your caption or offer. AIVideosUGC offers 6, 10, and 15 second jobs. Square images are the default still format.

input_guide.h2: Give the model a source that survives the crop

items.d: Photograph the product at the angle you want shoppers to remember. Include handles, lids, straps, and other parts that should remain visible.
Say whether the scene is a bathroom shelf, cafe table, closet rail, or outdoor bench so the background supports the product.
Leave breathing room around the item. A centered product gives you more options when Instagram previews a square post or covers the edges with interface elements.
Use a clean 1:1 image as the first feed post or carousel frame.
Show the product in use in a 9:16 clip for Reels or Stories, with the main action near the middle.
Add a close view of texture, hardware, packaging, or scale so the carousel answers a different question.

items.t: Routine Still — Serum at the Sink
items.d: Square still photo of an adult hand holding a serum bottle beside a bright sink while a single drop rests on the back of the other hand. Soft window light, natural beauty-photo detail, bottle and drop in sharp focus.

items.t: Try-On Still — Canvas Tote on Shoulder
items.d: Square still photo of an adult wearing a plain canvas tote over one shoulder at a cafe doorway, turning slightly so the front pocket is visible. Soft daylight, casual fashion styling, full tote in frame.

items.t: Product Detail Still — Single-Hole Phone Case
items.d: Square still photo of a plain dark silicone phone case with one small circular camera opening, held by an adult hand over a neutral surface. Keep the case edges, soft finish, and single opening clear in bright window light; no device or text.
Square still photo of adult hands lifting over-ear headphones from a plain box on a bright desk. Keep the headband and both earcups visible, with soft daylight and a clean top-down composition.
Type the product name, price, offer, and date in Instagram, Canva, CapCut, or Ads Manager instead of relying on generated lettering.
Add music or another permitted sound after download; AIVideosUGC does not add voiceover, music, or captions.
Open the finished Reel or Story preview and move added text away from profile controls, reply areas, and edge crops.
Use the caption to add details that do not belong inside the image, such as materials, sizing, or a shipping note.
